criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) (squamous and nonsquamous) with Stage IIIB/IIIC or Stage IV disease.
The participant has a programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression ≥ 50%.
The participant has measurable disease as defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1.
The participant has no prior systemic anti-tumor therapy for locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status 0-1.
The participant has any documented actionable genomic alteration (AGA) for which first-line (1L) approved therapies are indicated.
The participant has any symptomatic untreated central nervous system (CNS) metastases, leptomeningeal metastases (carcinomatous meningitis) or spinal cord compression.

The participant has any significant cardiovascular impairment as evidenced by uncontrolled hypertension (despite optimal medical treatment), congestive heart failure, active coronary disease (within 6 months prior to randomization), ventricular arrhythmias, or major thrombotic or embolic events or major hemorrhagic events (within 6 months prior to randomization), or significant risk of pulmonary hemorrhage.
The participant has an active autoimmune disease.

transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of Pumitamig Versus Pembrolizumab in Participants With Previously Untreated Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and PD-L1 ≥ 50%. (ROSETTA Lung-202)". Your earlier answers already covered 7 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been told you have a specific genetic change in your tumor (an actionable genomic alteration) that has a standard, approved treatment available as a first option?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't rightly know. I haven't heard of any specific genetic changes that have a standard treatment for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To check for significant heart or blood vessel issues, have you had uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart failure, heart disease, irregular heartbeats, or any major blood clots or bleeding events in the last 6 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, sir. I haven't had any of those heart or blood vessel problems in the last six months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: To be sure, have you had uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart failure, heart disease, irregular heartbeats, or major blood clots or bleeding in the last 6 months? It's okay if you're not sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, sir. I haven't had any of those heart or blood vessel problems in the last six months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
